devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This command assumes something important: people may rightly own things. There is
such a thing as what belongs to another, and it is to be respected.

But stealing is broader than taking goods. Scripture condemns dishonest scales
(Prov 11:1), withholding wages from a worker (Jas 5:4), and moving a neighbour's
boundary stone (Deut 19:14). Time taken from an employer, work not done that is
being paid for, ideas passed off as our own, taxes quietly evaded. All of it
belongs here.

Notice how Paul redirects a thief. He does not simply say stop. He writes,
"Anyone who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing
something useful with their own hands, that they may have something to share with
those in need" (Eph 4:28).

Look at the trajectory. From taking, to earning, to giving. The gospel does not
merely stop bad behaviour; it reverses direction entirely. The former thief
becomes a source of provision for others.

That is what grace does. It does not just remove; it replaces.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there anything you possess that is not honestly yours?
2. Where could you move from merely not taking to actively giving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, make me honest in small things as well as large. Turn my hands from
taking to giving. Amen.
